title: Factory Planning Card (RFC-0019 section 3.1)
description: One card on the CFactory planning board: the human-owned, editable unit of PLANNED work, served over `/api/cards`. A card is deliberately NOT a `work_items` row. `work_items` is a correlation store that CFactory reconciles and prunes from upstream completion events; a card carries fields no upstream event knows about (title, acceptance criteria, priority, milestone, assignee) and a reconcile would overwrite or drop them. The two live in separate tables and `correlation_key` is the join: NULL while the card is planned, set once the card enters the factory. This schema describes the card RESOURCE as served; `$defs.card_create` and `$defs.card_patch` describe the request bodies, and `$defs.card_list` the list response. Companion document: apis/planning-card.md. THIS FILE IS THE SOURCE OF TRUTH and it is hand-written, because most of what it carries is reasoning a generator cannot produce. It is not hand-RECONCILED: `scripts/check_planning_card_conformance.py` compares every `$def` below against the pydantic models in `cfactory.cards` on every CFactory pull request, and disagreement in either direction is a red build (Factory#554). Do not edit a field here without landing the matching model change, and do not edit a model without landing the matching change here.

card.description: The card resource as served by GET /api/cards/{card_key}. Every field below is emitted on every response - the nullable ones carry an explicit null rather than being omitted, so a consumer never has to distinguish `not set` from `not sent by this version of the server`. `required` lists the subset a VALIDATOR must insist on, which is narrower: the five fields carrying a model default (`description`, `repository_id`, `comment_count`, `comments_synced_at`, `deleted_at`) are always serialised but may be absent from a document being validated against this schema. Bounds are deliberately absent from this object and declared on the request bodies instead: the service enforces length limits when it ACCEPTS a value, not when it returns one, and a bound asserted here would be a rule nothing checks (Factory#554).

issue_state.description: The MIRRORED GitHub issue state (`open`/`closed`), read-only on the wire. NOT a card `status`: an issue can be closed while the card is still in review, and conflating the two is the mistake `status`'s enum exists to prevent. Stored in a 16-character column; that limit is not asserted here because no request body accepts this field, so nothing would ever validate against it.

labels.description: Labels mirrored from the GitHub issue. Read-only on the wire: the issue is the source of truth, and a card that could set them would silently diverge from it. Always an array - an unmirrored card carries `[]`, never null.

github_sync_error.description: Why the last sync with GitHub failed, or NULL when the last one succeeded. Present so a stale mirror is legible rather than looking like fresh data - the absence of an error and the absence of a sync are different states.

stage_runs.description: Per-stage idempotency records, keyed by stage. Read-only on the wire: it records what the factory was actually asked to do, so a caller must not be able to assert a dispatch that never happened. This is where per-stage idempotency lives now that `correlation_key` is deliberately reused across stages (RFC-0019 phase 7).

comment_count.description: How many comments are stored for this card. A scalar rather than the thread itself: a backlog of 46 cards each carrying a full thread is a payload nobody asked for (Factory#375). Never negative - it is the size of a set - but no `minimum` is asserted, because the value is server-computed (a correlated subquery on `card_comments`) and no request body accepts it, so the assertion would guard nothing.

comments_synced_at.description: When the thread was last read successfully, or NULL if it never has been. Read WITH `comment_count`: zero plus a timestamp means 'no discussion', zero plus NULL means 'we do not know' - which is the honest answer for an issue whose comments failed to download.

deleted_at.description: Soft-delete tombstone. Always NULL on anything a read hands back - a soft-deleted card is off the board. It is on the model because the import asks for a card BY ISSUE and has to be able to see the tombstone, rather than re-creating a card somebody deleted (RFC-0020 section 3.6).

created_at.description: When the card was created. Server-owned: set on POST and never mutable thereafter.

updated_at.description: When any field last changed. Server-owned: rewritten on every accepted mutation, including one made by a factory runtime writing status back.

card_key.description: Stable, human-quotable id. IMMUTABLE once issued - it is the path segment of every single-card route, so a rename would break every link a human or an agent has kept. Two origins, which is why there is no pattern here (Factory#371): the server assigns `FCT-<n>` from a per-tenant sequence when the caller supplies none, and a caller MAY supply its own key on create to mirror an id from an external tracker. A `^FCT-` pattern described only the first case and rejected the second, which the service accepts. Unique per tenant, not globally: two tenants may each legitimately run an FCT-1. Bounded at 128 characters, asserted on `card_create` where the service enforces it. Not the correlation key: see `correlation_key`.

tenant_id.description: Which tenant owns this card. Present in the resource so a consumer can assert what it is reading, but NEVER accepted from a request body: the server derives it from the calling credential (`CFACTORY_API_KEYS` / `CFACTORY_MULTI_TENANT`). Accepting it from the body would make cross-tenant writes a matter of typing a different string. Conventionally a lowercase slug of at most 64 characters (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}$`); that shape is documented rather than asserted, because the value is configured operationally and no code path validates it - a `pattern` here would have been a rule with no enforcer anywhere (Factory#554).

title.description: One line: what is to be done. Human-owned - no upstream event ever rewrites it. Non-empty and at most 512 characters, asserted on the request bodies where the service enforces it.

acceptance_criteria.description: What `done` means, one testable statement per entry. Human-owned. When the card dispatches (RFC-0019 section 3.2) these become the acceptance criteria of the RFC-0002 task contract, which is why an empty list is allowed while planning but a card dispatched without any gives the factory nothing to verify against. A blank entry is REFUSED on write: `card_create` and `card_patch` carry `minLength: 1` on the item and the service enforces it (CFactory#324) - an empty criterion is satisfied by anything, so it produces a green verdict against nothing, which reads like a check that ran. The bound sits on those two and NOT here, because it belongs where the service applies it - the request bodies - while this `$def` is also what the RESOURCE refs, and hundreds of cards predate the rule and still hold what they were created with. The service trims an entry before measuring it, so a single space is refused rather than stored.

status.description: Board column. `ready` is the dispatch trigger: a `ready` card WITH a `tier` is a first-class intake source alongside a labelled GitHub issue (RFC-0019 section 3.2). This vocabulary is the card's own and MUST NOT be classified through apis/status-taxonomy.json, which exists to normalise the four services' RUNTIME statuses: `ready` is a `done` token there and `blocked` is a `failed` token, so a card waiting to be picked up would read as finished and a card a human parked would read as a failure.

priority.description: Backlog order, LOWER IS HIGHER priority (0 is the top of the board). An integer rather than an enum so a card can be inserted between two others without renumbering the column, and NEGATIVE values are legal for exactly that reason - they are how a card jumps above 0 without rewriting every row beneath it (the board guide documents this; the schema previously said minimum 0 and the server never enforced it, Factory#371). Ties are legal; the server orders by (priority ASC, created_at ASC, card_key ASC) so a list is stable across requests. Defaults to 0 when omitted on create - i.e. a new card lands at the TOP of the backlog. The schema previously said 100; the service has always used 0 (Factory#554).

tier.description: RFC-0011 difficulty tier, the same vocabulary as the `factory:low|medium|hard` labels and the task contract's `execution.autonomy_tier`. Note `hard`, not `high`. NULL means not yet classified: the card is still a plan. The tier drives model, planning depth, human gate, VAL floor and merge behaviour once the card dispatches, so a `ready` card with a NULL tier is not dispatched - it stays on the board waiting for a human or an agent to classify it.

assignee.description: Who is on it: a human handle, or a factory runtime (`pfactory` / `aifactory` / `tfactory` / `cfactory`) once the card is in flight. Free-form because the board must be able to name a person who has no account here. NULL is unassigned. Bounded at 128 characters on the request bodies.

milestone.description: Milestone name this card belongs to, free-form. Deliberately a string and not a foreign key: the roadmap view groups by it, and RFC-0019 section 3.5 keeps GitHub authoritative, so this holds the GitHub milestone TITLE once card-to-issue mirroring lands (phase 6). NULL is unscheduled. Bounded at 128 characters on the request bodies.

correlation_key.description: RFC-0001 correlation key: the GitHub issue number as a string, or a synthetic <prefix>-<id>. THE JOIN between this card and the `work_items` timeline, and the reason the two are separate tables. NULL for as long as the card is only planned; set when the card enters the factory. NOT write-once. RFC-0019 phase 7 redefined this as the key the card's work is THREADED ON: a card runs through several stages, each an independent factory run, and they share the key deliberately - per-stage idempotency lives in `cards.stage_runs`, not in a one-shot key. The schema previously said a server MUST reject re-pointing, which is a design the fleet moved away from and which PATCH has never enforced (Factory#371). Bounded at 128 characters on the request bodies.

description.description: Free-text body. Carries the imported GitHub issue body when the card came from one (RFC-0020 phase 6), and is otherwise whatever a human typed. Distinct from `acceptance_criteria`, which is the testable list. Unbounded: an issue body is arbitrarily long and truncating one on import would silently lose what the card is about.

issue_ref.description: The GitHub issue this card mirrors, as `<owner>/<repo>#<number>`, or NULL for a card that has never been adopted. Writable on create and on PATCH: adopting an existing issue, or re-pointing at another, is a supported move (RFC-0020 phase 6). Unique per tenant in the store, so adopting an issue another card already mirrors is a 409. Bounded at 256 characters on the request bodies.

repository_id.description: Which of the tenant's repositories this card targets, or NULL for the tenant default (RFC-0020 section 3.3, phase 8). Writable on create and on PATCH, because re-targeting a planned card at another repository is a planning decision, not a migration.

card_create.description: POST /api/cards request body. `tenant_id`, `created_at` and `updated_at` are server-owned and are NOT accepted here - `tenant_id` in particular comes from the calling credential, and accepting it from a body would make a cross-tenant write a matter of typing a different string. Everything else the card carries that a caller can meaningfully originate IS accepted, including `card_key` (mirror an external tracker's id) and `correlation_key` (create a card that is already joined, which the GitHub import does). The mirrored fields - `issue_state`, `labels`, `github_sync_error`, `stage_runs` - are absent because GitHub and the dispatcher own them. Bounds are declared here rather than in the shared `$defs` because here is where the service enforces them. STRICTER THAN THE SERVICE, DELIBERATELY. `additionalProperties: false` says what a client MUST NOT send; the service today sets no pydantic `extra` policy, so it silently DISCARDS an unknown key instead of returning a 400 (measured, CFactory#322). That gap is a service bug and is tracked as one - the contract keeps the rule so a caller validating its own body still catches its own typo. This is the one direction in which this schema is allowed to lead the implementation: it may constrain what a CLIENT sends, and it may not assert anything about what the SERVER returns that the server does not actually guarantee (which is why every bound moved off `$defs.card` - Factory#554). Note that `scripts/check_planning_card_conformance.py` compares per FIELD and does not see object-level keywords, so this divergence is stated here rather than caught there.

card_patch.description: PATCH /api/cards/{card_key} request body: a partial card. Every mutable field may be sent, including `status` (move) and `priority` (reprioritise) - one route covers both, so an agent needs no special-case endpoints to do what a human does by dragging. Only the fields actually PRESENT in the request are applied, so `{"status": "done"}` moves a card and touches nothing else. `card_key` is absent: it is the path segment and the id other systems quote, so it is immutable. NOTE ON NULL: `scripts/check_planning_card_conformance.py` does not compare nullability on this object, because the service expresses `not sent` as `null` in the model and the two cannot be told apart from the outside - see that script's docstring. Where null is a real value here it clears the field (`tier`, `assignee`, `milestone`, `correlation_key`, `description`, `issue_ref`, `repository_id`); on `title`, `acceptance_criteria`, `status` and `priority` it is not, and the store rejects it. Sending no field at all is a mistake, not a no-op, hence `minProperties: 1` - and here too the contract leads the service, which accepts an empty body as a no-op (CFactory#322). STRICTER THAN THE SERVICE, DELIBERATELY. `additionalProperties: false` says what a client MUST NOT send; the service today sets no pydantic `extra` policy, so it silently DISCARDS an unknown key instead of returning a 400 (measured, CFactory#322). That gap is a service bug and is tracked as one - the contract keeps the rule so a caller validating its own body still catches its own typo. This is the one direction in which this schema is allowed to lead the implementation: it may constrain what a CLIENT sends, and it may not assert anything about what the SERVER returns that the server does not actually guarantee (which is why every bound moved off `$defs.card` - Factory#554). Note that `scripts/check_planning_card_conformance.py` compares per FIELD and does not see object-level keywords, so this divergence is stated here rather than caught there.

card_list.description: GET /api/cards response. An envelope rather than a bare array so pagination and echoed filters can be added additively later without breaking every consumer.

count.description: How many cards this response carries. Named `count`, not `total`: it is the length of `cards` in THIS response, not a total across pages. The schema said `total` while the service has always returned `count`, which is the drift Factory#371 found by hand and Factory#554 made impossible to reintroduce.

cards.description: Cards for the calling tenant only, ordered by (priority ASC, created_at ASC, card_key ASC).
